findings.title: NVD entry for CVE-2026-104935 (Ivanti Connect Secure authentication bypass)
findings.summary_md: NIST NVD published the CVE-2026-104935 entry on 13 October 2026, describing an authentication-bypass-by-spoofing vulnerability in Ivanti Connect Secure before version 25.1.3.0 that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands. The entry references the Ivanti vendor advisory and CISA KEV listing with an exploitation status of active and an automatable technical impact of total. It carries a CVSS 3.1 base score of 8.6 (HIGH) and lists affected version ranges including 25.1.0.0 through 25.1.1.2 and 22.8 R2 series.

findings.title: NVD entry for CVE-2026-106173 (Fortinet FortiSIEM path traversal)
findings.summary_md: NIST NVD published the CVE-2026-106173 record on 13 October 2026, identifying an improper path-traversal vulnerability in Fortinet FortiSIEM 7.5.0 (CPE 7.5.0, plus multiple 7.4.x, 7.3.x, 7.2.x, 7.1.x and 7.0.x ranges) that can allow attackers to execute unauthorized code or commands via specially crafted packets. The entry cites the Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-180 and assigns a CVSS 3.1 base score of 9.8 (CRITICAL) with network attack vector, no privileges required, and high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability.

findings.title: NVD entry for CVE-2026-109412 (Ivanti Neurons Patch for Intune exposed endpoint)
findings.summary_md: NIST NVD published the CVE-2026-109412 record on 13 October 2026, documenting an exposed dangerous endpoint in Ivanti Neurons Patch for Intune that allows a remote authenticated attacker to leak sensitive authentication information. The reference points to the Ivanti security advisory for October 2026. The CVSS 3.1 base score is 9.9 (CRITICAL) with changed scope, low privileges required, and high impact across confidentiality, integrity and availability.
